text:
raz: heads-up — p99 spike on streaming-chat after midnight deploy. users report choppy chunks. flame graphs point to host parse/tokenize + grpc writev. snapshot: https://perf.internal/runs/7995551 :grimacing:

cleo: which code landed? tokenizer or kernel selector changes?

raz: both. tokenizer now applies unicode fold + emoji collapse, and kernel metadata added a safety "compat" kernel for long seqs. perf top excerpt:
```
19.8% host::parse_stream
15.6% tokenizer::unicode_collapse
13.2% grpc::WriteV
11.0% kernel_selector::choose_compat_path
7.1% kvcache::evict_chain
5.4% http2::frame_write
```

mike: combo smell — tokenizer changes altered prefix hashes, kvcache misses -> more backend tokens, and compat kernel is slower. Mixed batches = worst-case.

ivy: short fixes:
- batch-split long sequences (max_mixed_batch=4)
- add debug logs for kernel selection reason and sampled batch seq_lens (1/500)
- add token_key_version metric and temporarily accept legacy-prefixes on miss for 5m window

raz: pushed canary for batch-split + kernel-reason logs. rolling now.

perf-bot: quick AB:
```
baseline: p95=118ms p99=230ms qps=460
canary: p95=130ms p99=270ms qps=440
canary+split: p95=120ms p99=235ms qps=455
```

cleo: good. longer-term items: kernel selector should be batch-composition aware (INF-2250), kvcache multi-version read window (INF-2251), and consider isolating >1k seq requests to dedicated workers.

mike: also bump grpc writev coalescing threshold to reduce syscall spikes for large streaming responses.

deploy-bot: canary started (deploy/799556). monitoring hooks enabled.

raz: update — canary+split dropped p99 ~35ms. leaving canary running and opening follow-ups. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
